title: VP Sara calls authorities’ actions involving her children ‘child abuse’
summary: Vice President Sara Duterte on Monday, Sept. 7, accused authorities of committing “child abuse” over their alleged presence near locations where her mother and children were staying, saying her…

blocks.text: Vice President Sara Duterte on Monday, Sept. 7, accused authorities of committing “child abuse” over their alleged presence near locations where her mother and children were staying, saying her family should not be used, threatened or dragged into any pressure against her. In a statement released by the Office of the Vice President (OVP), Duterte said she was particularly concerned about authorities approaching or going to locations where her family members, including minors, were staying. “Ang paglapit o pagpunta sa lugar kung saan naroroon ang aking ina at mga anak, sa kabila ng pag-amin ng DILG Secretary at ng pulisya na alam nila kung nasaan ako dahil sa kanilang surveillance activities, ay isang seryosong usapin, lalo na kung nadadamay o naaapektuhan ang mga menor de edad (Approaching or going to the place where my mother and children are, despite the admission of the DILG secretary and the police that they know where I am because of their surveillance activities, is a serious matter—especially when minors are affected or dragged into the situation),” Duterte said. “Ang mga bata ay hindi dapat ginagamit, tinatakot, o idinadamay sa panggigipit (Children must never be used, threatened, or dragged into harassment),” she said. “Ito ay child abuse (That is child abuse),” she added. READ: https://mb.com.ph/2026/09/05/i-do-not-feel-safe-vp-sara-fears-for-her-life-childrens-safety-after-arrest-warrant Security concerns Duterte said she had previously approached then-Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) Chief of Staff Gen. Romeo Brawner Jr. regarding her security, citing the constitutional line of succession. “Dahil ang aking seguridad ay nakaugnay sa Hukbong Sandatahan ng Pilipinas alinsunod sa constitutional line of succession, minabuti kong ipaalam sa dating Chief of Staff Gen. Romeo Brawner ang ilang mahahalagang pakiusap (Because my security is linked to the Armed Forces of the Philippines in accordance with the constitutional line of succession, I deemed it necessary to inform former Chief of Staff Gen. Romeo Brawner of several important requests),” Duterte said. “Higit sa lahat, hiniling ko na igalang at protektahan ang aking ina at mga anak, at huwag silang idamay o takutin sa kahit anumang gagawin sa akin (Above all, I asked that my mother and children be respected and protected, and that they not be dragged into or threatened by anything directed at me),” she added. Duterte also lamented that a government that fails to respect and protect children demonstrates a lack of concern for the country’s future. “Mga kababayan, ang isang pamahalaang hindi gumagalang at nagpoprotekta sa mga kabataan ay nagpapakita ng kawalan ng malasakit sa kinabukasan ng ating bayan (Fellow citizens, a government that does not respect and protect children reveals a lack of concern for the future of our nation),” Duterte said. Alleged plans date back to 2024 Duterte also claimed that she had received information as early as 2024 about alleged plans involving her and her father, former President Rodrigo Duterte. “Taong 2024 pa lamang ay umabot na sa akin ang impormasyon ng mga planong gawin ni Marcos (As early as 2024, information about Marcos’ plans had already reached me),” Duterte said. “Matagal na ako sa pampublikong serbisyo at nakahanda ako araw-araw sa posibilidad gawa ng aking trabaho (I have long been in public service, and I am prepared each day for the possibilities that come with my work),” she added. Duterte said the alleged plans included an International Criminal Court arrest warrant for her father and attacks against her. “Kabilang sa mga plano ang magkaroon ng ICC warrant kay dating Pangulong Duterte at ang mga gagawin na pag-atake sa akin (Among the plans were the issuance of an ICC warrant against former President Duterte and attacks directed at me),” she said. Surveillance allegations Duterte’s latest accusation followed her Sept. 5 allegations that the Marcos administration had been conducting surveillance and harassment operations against her and her family. She cited remarks from Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla, who said authorities knew her whereabouts the night before an arrest warrant was issued but did not immediately enforce it. Duterte said Remulla’s statement appeared to support documents she claimed her camp had long held regarding alleged surveillance and harassment operations by the Philippine National Police (PNP) and other government agencies. She also questioned why authorities allegedly went to her mother and children if government agencies already knew her whereabouts. “And because you know where I am, an important question you should answer is—why did you still need to go to my mother and children?” she said. She alleged that the purpose was to intimidate her family. “Isa lamang ang malinaw na sagot—upang takutin at sindakin ang aking pamilya (There is only one clear answer—to frighten and intimidate my family),” Duterte said. Duterte also said she did not trust the police and maintained that she could not surrender to authorities because she did not believe the government could guarantee her safety while in custody. She invoked the arrest and transfer of her father to the custody of the ICC, which she characterized as a “kidnapping” by the PNP. Duterte’s allegations come amid continuing political and legal tensions between her camp and the administration of President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., including disputes involving law enforcement, her family and legal proceedings.
